request:
Bless is to be a HIPAA compliant human in the loop service that works with AII ([AII])

The way it works with AII is via being a swift package add-on. It is designed to work with Sewn to be a human in the loop verification tool, such that when llm chat responses are about to be dispatched to a user they require approval from a third-party. Such as a patient talking to an LLM and their general practicitioner requiring to review the LLM response before it dispatches to the patient to confirm or modify the message for liability.

We will not integrate it with AII yet, but build it with it in mind such that Sewn can have it as an add-on.

It is also supposed to be designed to work any other customer's AI inference layer as AI APIs are standard in their approach of chat and response, Bless standardizes the human in the loop design.

----

After completing the initial approach of this build a site docs like Braid's: [Braid's docs/site]

That has a code explorer: [Braid's docs/EXPLORER.md]

with an ask orb. The ask orb works like VeilGarde's such that we use my mistral key locally, but it allows for users to use their own mistral key as it will boot without one and ask for one to use and ask questions to their codebase.

Just like braid generate a hero image that is brand consistent with braid's readme and place it in README_Assets prior to putting the hero image in Bless's README

The license for this framework should be GPL 3.0

and prepare it for public after completion

----

Build a testing macos app subpackage instead of a CLI to test with a mistral backend to also demo the standardizes human in the loop design pattern that dispatches to the bless framework

decisions.chose: Bless's pattern is one InferenceProvider wrapper, Blessed, not a hook inside Sewn
decisions.rejected: a hook in AII's Sewn now
decisions.reason: AII has no public seam on its response path; the request says not to integrate yet; a wrapper works with any chat layer today

decisions.chose: Two library products: Bless, with no networking, UI or logging, and BlessProviders, the chat-completions client
decisions.rejected: one module with the client inside
decisions.reason: the core stays usable on any transport and auditable for what it touches

decisions.chose: macOS 15 and iOS 18 for the library, macOS 26 for the playground, no upcoming-feature flags
decisions.rejected: macOS 26 only, as the family's MLX packages
decisions.reason: AII's floor is macOS 15 and a patient's app may be on a phone; the flags would change InferenceProvider's isolation for consumers

decisions.chose: The vocabulary: Draft, Petition, Verdict with a Ruling of bless, amend or withhold, Release, Gate, Seal, Ledger
decisions.reason: each word names one thing, and bless names the product

decisions.chose: The ledger holds ids, digests and enum codes, never content or free text
decisions.rejected: a free-text note field on events
decisions.reason: a withholding reason would put a diagnosis in the log every auditor reads; minimum necessary

decisions.chose: Signatures and hashes cover a versioned, length-prefixed byte layout, not JSON
decisions.reason: JSONEncoder's bytes for numbers, dates and escapes have changed across Foundation rewrites; a signature must outlive them

decisions.chose: Every timestamp is whole milliseconds, and JSON stores integer milliseconds
decisions.reason: ISO 8601 drops fractional seconds, so a verdict read back from disk would no longer verify

decisions.chose: Reviewers sign on their own device; the Gate takes a sealed Verdict and verifies it
decisions.rejected: the Gate signing with a private key it holds
decisions.reason: the Gate is the server; a reviewer's key should never leave the reviewer

decisions.chose: Named rules: withhold wins, blessings bind to the text, no stale verdicts, one blessing per reviewer per text, late is refused
decisions.reason: an amendment must be blessed as amended at quorum 2, and two reviewers acting at once must not bless different words

decisions.chose: Stores are synchronous, so the Gate's transitions never suspend
decisions.reason: every await inside an actor method is a reentrancy hole; synchronous stores make each transition and its ledger line one step

decisions.chose: Waiting is wake-and-recheck: a transition resumes every waiter with nothing, and each re-reads the store
decisions.reason: many waiters get the same release, none is resumed twice, and cancellation is simple

decisions.chose: Cancelling a waiting caller leaves the petition pending and writes nothing; only withdraw withdraws
decisions.reason: a dropped connection must not cancel a doctor's review

decisions.chose: The Gate owns no timer: sweep, lapse-on-entry and a self-waking wait with an injected sleeper
decisions.rejected: a background task inside the Gate
decisions.reason: a hidden timer cannot be paused or tested deterministically

decisions.chose: A lapse never releases the model's draft: hold, the default, withhold, or a fixed fallback text
decisions.rejected: releasing the draft at the deadline
decisions.reason: nothing unreviewed should ever reach a patient by default

decisions.chose: The SHA-256 value is named Sha256
decisions.reason: CryptoKit and swift-crypto both declare a Digest protocol; a Sewn file importing both would have to qualify every use

decisions.chose: SSE is parsed byte by byte
decisions.reason: the async line sequence drops blank lines, which end an event; checked on this Mac

decisions.chose: The playground is a SwiftUI app package with its Info.plist linked into the binary, built and exec'd by run.sh
decisions.rejected: a CLI, or an assembled .app bundle
decisions.reason: the request asks for an app; the linked plist gives a bundle id without a wrapper, the recipe Leviathan uses

decisions.chose: The playground's key resolves from its own Keychain item, MISTRAL_API_KEY, then ~/.rao/keys, through /usr/bin/security
decisions.reason: items written by security trust that tool and survive ad-hoc rebuilds; a plain key file is the wrong signal for a HIPAA demo

decisions.chose: Witnessed tees the draft to the operator's pane; the core has no UI hook
decisions.reason: the composition is the demo: a provider around a provider

decisions.reason: VeilGarde's is the newer port: whole-repository data, SPDX headers, and the ask orb that boots without a key

decisions.chose: The figures recompute the real fixtures: SiteFixturesTests writes one petition's ledger and seal
decisions.reason: a figure that recomputes Bless's own bytes cannot drift from the code

decisions.chose: The integration guide in two parts: the first party wraps the model and opens a review queue of four routes; the third party pulls the queue, signs in the browser with Web Crypto, and posts the verdict

decisions.chose: The queue's items carry the petition with its current message and digest, and the POST route accepts a verdict only for the signed-in reviewer
decisions.reason: a petition's JSON holds its stored fields, not the derived text and digest a verdict must name

decisions.chose: ARCHITECTURE.md and Docs/examples are ignored and untracked, kept on the owner's Mac; public links point at the site and the guide

decisions.chose: The README and the run page close on Rilke's rest between two notes, from the Book of Hours: the reviewer as the pause in which the model's reply and the patient are reconciled. The English is this run's rendering of the German, with the line about Death left out

decisions.chose: Every Swift file's header names its author and copyright after its license: Created by Ritesh Pakala on the day the file was first added, and Copyright © 2026 Rao Studios LLC. The license stays on the fourth line, the manifests' on the second, and PackageLayeringTests holds both

assumptions.text: HIPAA compliant means built to support the Security Rule's technical safeguards and minimum necessary, with the deployer's part named; no library is compliant on its own.
One reviewer per petition in the playground; the library supports a quorum of several.
The model provider used with real patient data has a business associate agreement, or is a model the clinic runs itself.

questions.text: Should the quorum become cryptographic, a k-of-n release over a content key, so even the host cannot release early? It is open.
Should the policy's context window default to a small number of messages, for minimum necessary, rather than the whole conversation?
Where should the ledger's head hash be anchored, so a replaced ledger is detectable?
